rows.ARS:
Russet Miniature.
Registration name: SAVabear
Exhibition name: Teddy Bear ™
rows.Origin:
Bred by F. Harmon Saville (1924-1997) (United States, before 1989).
Introduced in United States by Nor' East Miniature Roses as 'Teddy Bear'.
rows.Bloom: Russet. Mild fragrance. 28 petals. Average diameter 0.75". Small, very double bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season.
rows.Habit:
Compact, upright, well-branched.

Height: 14" to 20" (35 to 50cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 5b through 11. Can be used for beds and borders, container rose, garden or specimen. Vigorous. flowers drop off cleanly. Disease susceptibility: very disease resistant. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that. Requires spring freeze protection (see glossary - Spring freeze protection) .

Miniature rose plant named Savabear

F. Harmon Saville, Rowley, Massachusetts

... A new and unusual orange brown russet miniature... Parentage: 'Sachet' x 'Rainbow's End'... Blooming habit: Continuous... Bloom Size: about .75 inches... No. of Petals: 28... Petals drop off cleanly... Fragrance: Slight... Flowers are long lasting on plant and as cut flower... Hips: Globular... Height: 14 to 16 inches... Average resistance to disease... Needs winter protection in severe climates...
rows.Notes: Justice Miniature Roses says this rose is the closest to a true brown of all their russet offerings... it is disease resistant, but will require protection when the weather turns cold...
